title: Linked lists and pointers
summary: Nodes connected by arrows. Reverse one with three pointers.

cards.title: A treasure hunt
cards.body:
An array is a row of lockers side by side. A **linked list** is a treasure hunt: each clue (a **node**) holds a value and tells you where the next clue is. That "where" is a **pointer**: a memory address.

The last node points to `nullptr`, which means "nothing here".

cards.title: Who owns the memory?
cards.body:
In this app's code the nodes live in a `std::vector`, which **owns** them. The `next` pointers only **point**; they don't own anything.

Always ask "who owns this memory, and who frees it?" It's the single most important question in C++.
Watch the arrows flip one at a time. The labels above the nodes show where `prev`, `curr` and `next` point.

cards.title: The code
cards.body: The order of the four lines is everything. If you flip `curr->next` **before** saving it, the rest of the list is lost forever. That's a **memory leak** (with `new`) or just a broken list.

cards.title: Arrays vs lists in games
cards.body:
Lists can insert or remove a node in O(1) if you already have a pointer to the spot. Arrays need O(n) shifting.

But arrays keep values **next to each other** in memory, and the CPU loves that (its cache loads neighbours for free). List nodes can be scattered, so walking a list is often much slower in practice. That's why game engines prefer arrays and use lists mainly for things like **free lists** in object pools.

cards.question: In `reverseList`, what goes wrong if you swap the first two lines inside the loop (flip `curr->next = prev` before saving `next`)?
choices: You lose the pointer to the rest of the list
cards.explain: After `curr->next = prev`, the old `curr->next` is overwritten and nothing else remembers where the rest of the list was.

cards.question: Getting the 500th element: array vs linked list?
cards.explain: An array computes the address directly (`start + 500 × size`). A list must follow 500 arrows.

cards.title: Build it: reverse a list
cards.body: Write `reverseList` yourself. Draw the boxes and arrows on paper for 3 nodes before typing anything.
